title: Suffixes and parts of speech
lede: The ending of a word usually tells you what job it does in a sentence.

sections.md:
## Why endings matter
One root can become a noun, a verb, an adjective and an adverb just by changing the ending: **profit, profitable, profitably, profiteer**. If you know the root and recognize the ending, you know the word.

## Noun endings (things, people, ideas)
| Suffix | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| -tion, -sion | act or state of | negotiation, decision |
| -ment | result or act of | payment, agreement |
| -ness | state of being | awareness, darkness |
| -ity, -ty | quality of | reliability, loyalty |
| -er, -or, -ist | person who | driver, investor, analyst |
| -ance, -ence | state of | compliance, persistence |

## Adjective endings (describing words)
| Suffix | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| -able, -ible | can be | profitable, flexible |
| -ful | full of | careful, successful |
| -less | without | reckless, fearless |
| -ous, -ious | having | dangerous, ambitious |
| -ive | tending to | aggressive, productive |
| -al, -ic | relating to | financial, strategic |

## Verb and adverb endings
| Suffix | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| -ize, -ise | to make | finalize, prioritize |
| -ify | to make | simplify, verify |
| -en | to make | strengthen, widen |
| -ate | to do or cause | negotiate, activate |
| -ly (adverb) | in a way that is | quickly, carefully |

sections.title: Building a word family
steps: Noun: reli**ability** (the quality of being reliable).

practice.why: -ence makes a state or quality: a noun.

practice.q: A "meticulous" person is ___. Which part of speech is meticulous?

practice.why: -ly turns an adjective into an adverb.
-ible = can be. Feasible = able to be done.

practice.q: Fill the blank: "We need to ___ the loads by delivery time."
practice.why: The sentence needs a verb; -ize makes one.
